channel.title: The Local Europe - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local Europe (thelocal.com)

item.title: EU announces new push to overhaul visa system and deportations policy
item.description: The European Union on Thursday laid out plans to overhaul its visa system and step up deportations as part of a five-year migration strategy that cements a hardening line on the hot-button issue.

item.title: Four international night trains from Germany to try in 2026
item.description: Several new night trains will bring passengers from Germany to popular cities around Europe this year, and a couple of popular connections that were set to end are being saved. Here are four exciting overnight journeys to ride this year.

item.title: French island offers up to €10,000 to second-home owners who rent out their property
item.description: Local officials on a French island are offering incentives of up to €10,000 to second-home owners who are willing to rent out their properties on a long-term lease, in order to try and overcome the housing shortage for locals.

item.title: EU announces plan to extend 90-day rule for certain non-EU workers
item.description: The European Commission has announced it will look into allowing certain non-EU professionals to stay in the EU beyond the current 90/180-day rule, as part of a future overhaul of its visa system. It also asked EU countries to make visa access "simpler and faster" for skilled workers.

item.title: OPINION: German school grading is unfair on foreign students and it's maddening
item.description: Student participation, called 'Mitarbeit', makes up a large portion of students' grades in German schools. But the way it's assessed can be poison in the classroom, particularly for foreign pupils, writes Tom Pugh.

item.title: OPINION: PM has steadied France, but sacrificed any hope of cutting the deficit
item.description: Prime minister Sébastien Lecornu has, through compromise and concession got his budget passed. John Lichfield says that Lecornu will likely remain prime minister until spring 2027 - but while he has steadied the ship, he has sacrificed all hope of tackling France's ballooning deficit.

item.title: What’s a good salary in Germany in 2026?
item.description: If you’re eyeing a career move to Germany or already living here as a foreign resident, 2026 is shaping up to be an intriguing and largely positive year for salaries.

item.title: EU delays full rollout of EES border system over travel chaos concerns
item.description: The deadline for the full implementation of the Europe's Entry/Exit System (EES), the new EU digital border system, has been postponed from April to September amid concerns over travel disruptions during the summer season, a European Commission spokesperson said on Friday.

item.title: Inside France: Family-friendly France, American tech boycott and Minitel
item.description: From the ongoing game of musical chairs that is French politics right now to the move to replace American tech with French products, via France's family-friendly reputation, Inside France is our weekly look at the latest news and talking points from France.

item.title: Spain PM defends migration policy from Musk criticism
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez on Friday defended his leftist government's plan to grant legal status to hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants after criticism from billionaire tycoon Elon Musk.
